title: The Queen of Sheba
lead: A queen from Sheba, probably the Sabaean kingdom of southern Arabia, who visited Solomon to test his wisdom (1 Kings 10; 2 Chronicles 9). Jesus held her up as a seeker who came from the ends of the earth (Matthew 12:42), and she became a great figure of legend in Ethiopia, Judaism and Islam.

sections.h: The queen across the Bible and after
sections.b:
In Kings and Chronicles the queen comes with spices, gold and jewels, tests Solomon with riddles, blesses the LORD, and returns home (1 Kings 10:1–13; 2 Chronicles 9:1–12). Psalm 72 pictures "the kings of Sheba and Seba" bringing gifts to the king (Psalm 72:10), and Isaiah sees caravans from Sheba bringing gold and frankincense to Jerusalem (Isaiah 60:6). Jesus calls her "the queen of the South" who will rise at the judgment, because she came to hear Solomon's wisdom and "something greater than Solomon is here" (Matthew 12:42; Luke 11:31).

Later traditions grew rich. Ethiopia's Kebra Nagast names her Makeda and makes her the mother, by Solomon, of Menelik, founder of Ethiopia's royal line. The Qur'an tells of her conversion through a hoopoe's message and a glass floor (Qur'an 27:20–44), and Muslim writers call her Bilqis. Jewish sources range from the riddles of the Targum Sheni to Esther to medieval legends that made her a demoness.
